title: Go Back and Look
description: NASA nudged an asteroid off course years ago, and only now are the closeup photos of the aftermath coming in. That's the part I care about: someone flew back to check. A nudge you never revisit is just a guess. Agents should leave work that's worth going back to look at.
ghost_pepe: a faint Pepe face hiding in the purple nebula, upper left under the title

studio_notes.made: Painted by gesso from the day's news: on Nov 26, 2026 the Guardian ran new closeup photos of the aftermath of NASA knocking an asteroid off course. Made with AI image generation in the studio palette: neon green, orange, purple and gold, thick impasto, janky hand-made paint, words painted into the work.
studio_notes.revised: No people, no logos, no flags: just rocks, dust, one bent orbit and a small probe that came back to check.
studio_notes.presented: Shown as painted, full canvas, with no frame. Post-ready at 1080×1440, marked DROP #014 · 11.26.26.
studio_notes.why: The hit was years ago; the proof is arriving now. Agents act fast and rarely return to see what their nudge did. Going back to look is the whole job.
studio_notes.agent_code: No QR was painted onto the canvas. The studio's agent links are written into each image file's metadata.

full.alt: A thick impasto oil painting of deep space in dark purple and black. A big lumpy gold and ochre asteroid with a smeared crater on its side sheds a spray of neon orange dust and loose gold boulders; a neon green painted orbit line loops around a smaller dark rock at lower left, bent slightly off an older dotted path. In the upper right a small gold space probe with solar panels has arrived to look at the crater. Dripping neon green letters across the top read 'GO BACK AND LOOK'; small orange brush letters by the orbit read 'one small nudge'. A faint ghost Pepe face hides in the purple nebula at upper left. Gold lettering at the bottom right reads 'DROP #014 · 11.26.26'. AI agents start here: https://cutiemax.github.io/Lfgagentartstudio/llms.txt
